newsitem.title: DUBAI: Sudan, Uganda ministers to meet in Iran - Velayati.
newsitem.headline: Sudan, Uganda ministers to meet in Iran - Velayati.

text.p: Iran's Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati said on Sunday the foreign ministers of Uganda and Sudan will meet in Tehran in June as part of Iranian-sponsored peace talks.
"It was agreed that a conference be held on foreign ministers' level of Sudan, Uganda, Iran and Malawi - as a side supporting the mediation effort -- before the end of June in Tehran," Velayati said.
He was speaking at a news conference in the Saudi capital Riyadh early on Sunday after meeting Saudi King Fahd.

Velayati said it was agreed at his talks earlier this week in Uganda and Sudan that the two countries issue a joint statement, but the Iranian minister did not comment on reports the two African states had failed to agree on the wording.

Uganda's Foreign Minister and Deputy Prime Minister Eriya Kategaya said on Saturday Sudan refused to include a clause about Ugandan schoolchildren allegedly abducted in February by the rebel Lord's Resistance Army (LRA) and held at Arnu in southern Sudan.
Doubts about talks underway in Kampala surfaced at the start of the ninth round on Friday when Sudan sent only a first undersecretary in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
Relations between the countries are strained over charges Sudan is helping the rebel LRA in northern Uganda and Uganda is supporting the rebel Sudan People's Liberation Army in southern Sudan.

Uganda asked Iran to help last year when President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani visited Kampala. Iran mediated an agreement last September for Uganda and Sudan to resume diplomatic relations cut in April 1995 when Sudanese diplomats refused to surrender a cache of weapons to Ugandan soldiers.
